------------------------------ MODULE W4Od17m7p0t1 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Routers, None, MaxCS

VARIABLES reg, granted, inflight, csCount, lastOwner

vars == <<reg, granted, inflight, csCount, lastOwner>>

Acquiring(r) == [rtr |-> r, exp |-> None, new |-> r]
Releasing(r) == [rtr |-> r, exp |-> r,    new |-> None]

HasPending(r) == \E m \in inflight : m.rtr = r

Init ==
    /\ reg = None
    /\ granted = [r \in Routers |-> FALSE]
    /\ inflight = {}
    /\ csCount = 0
    /\ lastOwner = None

Request(r) ==
    /\ granted[r] = FALSE
    /\ ~HasPending(r)
    /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {Acquiring(r)}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, granted, csCount, lastOwner>>

ApplyAcquire(m) ==
    /\ m \in inflight
    /\ m.new = m.rtr
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
    /\ IF reg = m.exp
          THEN /\ reg' = m.rtr
               /\ granted' = [granted EXCEPT ![m.rtr] = TRUE]
               /\ csCount' = csCount + 1
               /\ lastOwner' = m.rtr
          ELSE UNCHANGED <<reg, granted, csCount, lastOwner>>

ReleaseReq(r) ==
    /\ granted[r] = TRUE
    /\ ~HasPending(r)
    /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {Releasing(r)}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, granted, csCount, lastOwner>>

ApplyRelease(m) ==
    /\ m \in inflight
    /\ m.new = None
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
    /\ IF reg = m.exp
          THEN /\ reg' = None
               /\ granted' = [granted EXCEPT ![m.rtr] = FALSE]
               /\ UNCHANGED <<csCount, lastOwner>>
          ELSE UNCHANGED <<reg, granted, csCount, lastOwner>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Routers : Request(r)
    \/ \E r \in Routers : ReleaseReq(r)
    \/ \E m \in inflight : ApplyAcquire(m)
    \/ \E m \in inflight : ApplyRelease(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ArmHeldMatchesRegister ==
    \A r \in Routers : granted[r] => (reg = r)

BoundedCS == csCount <= MaxCS

================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Routers = {r1, r2}
    None = None
    MaxCS = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ArmHeldMatchesRegister
CONSTRAINT BoundedCS
nl:
An airport baggage-router network coordinates several routers that all want exclusive use of a single sorting arm. Ownership of the arm is decided by a compare-and-swap register: a router that wants the arm posts a CAS request that says "if the register currently reads free, set it to me." Because the control bus reorders traffic, posted requests sit in an in-flight pool and can be applied to the register in any order, not the order they were posted. When a request is applied the register is inspected: the swap takes effect only if the register still holds the exact value the request expected, otherwise the request is discarded with no effect. A router that observes its swap succeed marks itself as holding the arm and later posts a release request that swaps the register back to free. Every successful acquisition also bumps a critical-section counter and records the last owner, so the audit trail is preserved. The whole point of the compare-and-swap discipline is that reordered, racing requests can never let two routers believe they hold the arm at once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a router is marked as holding the sorting arm, the compare-and-swap register reads exactly that router's identity, so no two routers can simultaneously hold the arm.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od6m3p0t5 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, Admins, None, MaxTerm, MaxDispatch, MaxOverride

VARIABLES term, leader, ctlState, dispatched, overrides

vars == <<term, leader, ctlState, dispatched, overrides>>

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = None
    /\ ctlState = [c \in Controllers |-> "follower"]
    /\ dispatched = 0
    /\ overrides = 0

StartElection(c) ==
    /\ leader = None
    /\ ctlState[c] \in {"follower", "candidate"}
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ ctlState' = [ctlState EXCEPT ![c] = "candidate"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, dispatched, overrides>>

WinElection(c) ==
    /\ ctlState[c] = "candidate"
    /\ leader = None
    /\ leader' = c
    /\ ctlState' = [ctlState EXCEPT ![c] = "leader"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, dispatched, overrides>>

Dispatch(c) ==
    /\ leader = c
    /\ ctlState[c] = "leader"
    /\ dispatched' = dispatched + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, ctlState, overrides>>

Fail(c) ==
    /\ ctlState[c] = "leader"
    /\ ctlState' = [ctlState EXCEPT ![c] = "failed"]
    /\ leader' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, dispatched, overrides>>

Recover(c) ==
    /\ ctlState[c] = "failed"
    /\ ctlState' = [ctlState EXCEPT ![c] = "follower"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, dispatched, overrides>>

AdminOverride(a, c) ==
    /\ leader' = c
    /\ ctlState' = [d \in Controllers |->
                       IF d = c THEN "leader"
                       ELSE IF ctlState[d] = "leader" THEN "follower"
                       ELSE ctlState[d]]
    /\ overrides' = overrides + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, dispatched>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : StartElection(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : WinElection(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Dispatch(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Fail(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Recover(c)
    \/ \E a \in Admins, c \in Controllers : AdminOverride(a, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AtMostOneLeader ==
    \A c \in Controllers : ctlState[c] = "leader" => leader = c

BoundState ==
    /\ term <= MaxTerm
    /\ dispatched <= MaxDispatch
    /\ overrides <= MaxOverride

================================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {e1, e2, e3}
    Admins = {adm}
    None = None
    MaxTerm = 3
    MaxDispatch = 2
    MaxOverride = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AtMostOneLeader
CONSTRAINT BoundState
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper is run by several controllers, but only one may hold leadership of the shared dispatch bus at any moment. Leadership is decided by election terms: when there is no leader a controller can start a new election, bumping the term and becoming a candidate, and a candidate may win the election only while the leadership slot is still vacant, at which point it becomes the leader. The leader may dispatch cars, and a leader can fail, which vacates the leadership slot and lets a failover election run; a failed controller can later recover to a follower. A privileged building admin can override the normal protocol and forcibly install any controller as leader, which simultaneously demotes whichever controller was previously leader back to follower. Because the leadership slot is a single shared value and every path that marks a controller as leader also writes that controller into the slot, the controller-state view and the slot can never disagree. That guarantee is what enforces mutual exclusion of the dispatch bus.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a controller is in the leader state, the shared leadership slot names exactly that controller, so at most one controller ever holds the dispatch bus.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od2m0p3t1 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Robots, Slots, None, MaxVer

VARIABLES version, owner, reads, pending, claimed

vars == <<version, owner, reads, pending, claimed>>

HasSnap(r) == \E m \in reads   : m.rob = r
HasPend(r) == \E m \in pending : m.rob = r

Init ==
    /\ version = [s \in Slots  |-> 0]
    /\ owner   = [s \in Slots  |-> None]
    /\ reads   = {}
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ claimed = [r \in Robots |-> None]

Read(r, s) ==
    /\ claimed[r] = None
    /\ ~HasSnap(r)
    /\ ~HasPend(r)
    /\ owner[s] = None
    /\ reads' = reads \cup {[rob |-> r, slot |-> s, ver |-> version[s]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, owner, pending, claimed>>

Commit(m) ==
    /\ m \in reads
    /\ reads'   = reads \ {m}
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, owner, claimed>>

ApplyCommit(m) ==
    /\ m \in pending
    /\ pending' = pending \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED reads
    /\ IF version[m.slot] = m.ver /\ owner[m.slot] = None
          THEN /\ owner'   = [owner   EXCEPT ![m.slot] = m.rob]
               /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![m.slot] = @ + 1]
               /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![m.rob]  = m.slot]
          ELSE UNCHANGED <<owner, version, claimed>>

Release(r) ==
    /\ claimed[r] # None
    /\ owner'   = [owner   EXCEPT ![claimed[r]] = None]
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![claimed[r]] = @ + 1]
    /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![r] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reads, pending>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots, s \in Slots : Read(r, s)
    \/ \E m \in reads   : Commit(m)
    \/ \E m \in pending : ApplyCommit(m)
    \/ \E r \in Robots  : Release(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

DoubleAllocationFree ==
    \A r \in Robots : claimed[r] # None => owner[claimed[r]] = r

BoundedVersion == \A s \in Slots : version[s] <= MaxVer

================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Robots = {a, b}
    Slots = {s1, s2}
    None = None
    MaxVer = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT DoubleAllocationFree
CONSTRAINT BoundedVersion
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shares a rack of storage slots, and each robot wants to claim an empty slot without colliding with another robot. Claiming uses optimistic locking: a robot first reads a slot's current version number while the slot is free, holds that version as a snapshot, and later submits a commit that carries the version it saw. Because the fleet radio delivers commit messages out of order, submitted commits sit in a pending pool and the controller applies them in any order. When a commit is applied the slot's live version is compared against the snapshot the commit carries: the claim takes effect only if the version is still unchanged and the slot is still free, and otherwise the commit is rejected and the robot must read and retry. A successful claim writes the robot as the slot's owner, bumps the slot version, and records which slot that robot now holds. Releasing a slot clears the owner and bumps the version again. The optimistic-locking discipline exists so that two robots racing for the same slot can never both come away believing they own it.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a robot records that it holds a slot, that slot's owner field names exactly that robot, so no slot is ever double-allocated to two robots.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od11m2p1t2 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Txns, Instances, None

VARIABLES record, committed, phase, lockedBy, initiator

vars == <<record, committed, phase, lockedBy, initiator>>

RECURSIVE SumAmounts(_)
SumAmounts(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
         IN x + SumAmounts(S \ {x})

Init ==
    /\ record = 0
    /\ committed = {}
    /\ phase = [t \in Txns |-> "idle"]
    /\ lockedBy = None
    /\ initiator = [t \in Txns |-> None]

Prepare(t, i) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "idle"
    /\ lockedBy = None
    /\ lockedBy' = t
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "prepared"]
    /\ initiator' = [initiator EXCEPT ![t] = i]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, committed>>

Commit(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "prepared"
    /\ lockedBy = t
    /\ record' = record + t
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {t}
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "committed"]
    /\ lockedBy' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED initiator

Abort(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "prepared"
    /\ lockedBy = t
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "aborted"]
    /\ lockedBy' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, committed, initiator>>

Retry(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "aborted"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
    /\ initiator' = [initiator EXCEPT ![t] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, committed, lockedBy>>

Quiesce ==
    /\ \A t \in Txns : phase[t] = "committed"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Txns, i \in Instances : Prepare(t, i)
    \/ \E t \in Txns : Commit(t)
    \/ \E t \in Txns : Abort(t)
    \/ \E t \in Txns : Retry(t)
    \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdate == record = SumAmounts(committed)

================================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Txns = {1, 2, 3}
    Instances = {c1, c2}
    None = None
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A print-shop job spooler keeps a single shared page-count record that transactions update by adding their job's page total. Two spooler coordinator instances share the one pool of participants, so both can start transactions that contend for the shared record. Updates use two-phase commit: a transaction first prepares, which grabs an exclusive pool lock so only one transaction is in flight at a time, and records which coordinator instance is driving it. From the prepared state a transaction either commits, adding its page amount to the record and releasing the lock, or aborts, releasing the lock with no change. An aborted transaction can reset back to idle and be retried later. Because only a prepared, lock-holding transaction may commit, and a committed transaction can never prepare again, every committed transaction's page amount is added exactly once and none is overwritten. The record must therefore always equal the exact sum of the page amounts of the transactions that have committed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared page-count record always equals the sum of the page amounts of exactly the transactions that have committed, so no committed update is ever lost.

VARIABLES blockReg, inBlock, slow, requested, moves

    /\ slow = [t \in Trains |-> FALSE]
    /\ requested = [t \in Trains |-> FALSE]

Request(t) ==

    /\ inBlock[t] = FALSE
    /\ requested' = [requested EXCEPT ![t] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<blockReg, inBlock, slow, moves>>

BecomeSlow(t) ==

    /\ slow' = [slow EXCEPT ![t] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<blockReg, inBlock, requested, moves>>

Resume(t) ==
    /\ slow[t] = TRUE
    /\ slow' = [slow EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<blockReg, inBlock, requested, moves>>

Enter(t) ==
    /\ requested[t] = TRUE
    /\ slow[t] = FALSE
    /\ blockReg = None
    /\ blockReg' = t
    /\ inBlock' = [inBlock EXCEPT ![t] = TRUE]
    /\ requested' = [requested EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
    /\ moves' = moves + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED slow

Leave(t) ==
    /\ inBlock[t] = TRUE
    /\ blockReg = t
    /\ blockReg' = None
    /\ inBlock' = [inBlock EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slow, requested, moves>>

    \/ \E t \in Trains : BecomeSlow(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Resume(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Enter(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Leave(t)

CONSTANTS
    Trains = {x1, x2, x3}
    None = None
    MaxMoves = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OccupantConsistent
CONSTRAINT BoundedMoves
nl:
A subway signalling system protects a single-track block that only one train may occupy at a time. Occupancy is arbitrated by a compare-and-swap register that names the current occupant or reads free. A train that wants the block first raises a request. A train may also be slow: signalling delays can put a train into a slow state in which it cannot act on the register, and it later resumes to normal; slowness only delays a train, it never fails or vanishes. To enter, a non-slow requesting train performs a compare-and-swap that succeeds only if the register still reads free, in which case the register is set to that train, the train marks itself as occupying the block, and a movement counter advances. Leaving the block swaps the register back to free and clears the train's occupying mark. Because a train marks itself occupying only on a compare-and-swap that found the register free and wrote its own identity, the occupying view can never disagree with the register.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a train marks itself as occupying the block, the compare-and-swap register names exactly that train, so two trains can never occupy the block at once.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od6m6p1t2 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Instances, Updates, None, LeaseTicks

VARIABLES record, holder, leaseTime, applied, pending

vars == <<record, holder, leaseTime, applied, pending>>

Init ==
    /\ record = 0
    /\ holder = None
    /\ leaseTime = 0
    /\ applied = {}
    /\ pending = Updates

Grant(i) ==
    /\ holder = None
    /\ holder' = i
    /\ leaseTime' = LeaseTicks
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, applied, pending>>

Apply(i, u) ==
    /\ holder = i
    /\ leaseTime > 0
    /\ u \in pending
    /\ applied' = applied \cup {u}
    /\ pending' = pending \ {u}
    /\ record' = record + u
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, leaseTime>>

Tick(i) ==
    /\ holder = i
    /\ leaseTime > 0
    /\ leaseTime' = leaseTime - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, holder, applied, pending>>

Expire ==
    /\ holder # None
    /\ leaseTime = 0
    /\ holder' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, leaseTime, applied, pending>>

Idle ==
    /\ holder = None
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Grant(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, u \in Updates : Apply(i, u)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Tick(i)
    \/ Expire
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

RECURSIVE SumWeights(_)
SumWeights(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN x + SumWeights(S \ {x})

NoLostUpdate == record = SumWeights(applied)

CONSTANTS
    Instances = {c1, c2}
    Updates = {1, 2, 3}
    None = None
    LeaseTicks = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
An elevator bank keeps a single shared configuration record that its two coordinator instances both update, drawing coordination rights from one shared pool. Write access is governed by a lease: the pool grants a lease to one instance for a bounded number of ticks, and only the current lease holder may apply updates to the record. Each update a holder applies adds that update's weight to the record and marks the update as applied so it is never applied twice. A lease counts down on every tick and, once it reaches zero, expires and returns the pool to the free state so another instance may take a lease; updates already applied stay in the record across lease changes. Because only the single current lease holder can write, and applied updates are recorded once and never overwritten, the record can never drop or double-count a committed update. The shared record therefore always equals the exact total weight of the updates that have been applied.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared configuration record always equals the summed weight of exactly the updates marked applied, so no committed update is ever lost or overwritten.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od13m4p3t2 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS JobIds, Columns, Instances, None, QCap

VARIABLES queue, owner, holds, finished

vars == <<queue, owner, holds, finished>>

InQueue(id) == \E k \in 1..Len(queue) : queue[k].id = id

Init ==
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ owner = [c \in Columns |-> None]
    /\ holds = [j \in JobIds |-> None]
    /\ finished = {}

Enqueue(id, col, i) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < QCap
    /\ ~InQueue(id)
    /\ holds[id] = None
    /\ id \notin finished
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, [id |-> id, col |-> col])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, holds, finished>>

Allocate(i) ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ LET j == Head(queue) IN
         /\ owner[j.col] = None
         /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![j.col] = j.id]
         /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![j.id] = j.col]
         /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED finished

DropHead ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ owner[Head(queue).col] # None
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, holds, finished>>

Finish(id) ==
    /\ holds[id] # None
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![holds[id]] = None]
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![id] = None]
    /\ finished' = finished \cup {id}
    /\ UNCHANGED queue

Idle ==
    /\ Len(queue) = 0
    /\ \A id \in JobIds : id \in finished
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E id \in JobIds, col \in Columns, i \in Instances : Enqueue(id, col, i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Allocate(i)
    \/ DropHead
    \/ \E id \in JobIds : Finish(id)
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A id \in JobIds : holds[id] # None => owner[holds[id]] = id

================================================================================
nl:
A vending-machine network dispenses from a shared pool of product columns, driven by two dispatcher instances that both feed one bounded work queue. Customer dispense jobs are enqueued into the queue, but the queue applies backpressure: if it already holds its capacity of jobs, further enqueues are refused until space frees. A dispatcher pulls the head job off the queue and tries to allocate the column that job targets; the allocation succeeds only if that column is currently unassigned, in which case the column records this job as its owner and the job records which column it holds. A job that cannot get its column is dropped from the queue. When a job finishes, its column is released back to unassigned. Because a column is assigned to a job only while it is unassigned, and each job records at most the one column it actually holds, two jobs can never both hold the same column. The queue never exceeds its capacity, and no product column is ever double-allocated.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a job records that it holds a column, that column's owner field names exactly that job, so no column is ever allocated to two jobs at once.

VARIABLES capacity, free, allocated, leader, regState

    /\ free = 2
    /\ allocated = 0

    /\ regState = [r \in Registrars |-> "follower"]

    /\ regState[r] = "follower"

    /\ regState' = [regState EXCEPT ![r] = "leader"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, free, allocated>>

    /\ regState' = [regState EXCEPT ![r] = "follower"]
    /\ leader' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, free, allocated>>

Enroll(r) ==
    /\ leader = r
    /\ free > 0
    /\ free' = free - 1
    /\ allocated' = allocated + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, leader, regState>>

Drop(r) ==
    /\ leader = r
    /\ allocated > 0
    /\ allocated' = allocated - 1
    /\ free' = free + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, leader, regState>>

RaiseCapacity ==
    /\ capacity + Step <= MaxCap
    /\ capacity' = capacity + Step
    /\ free' = free + Step
    /\ UNCHANGED <<allocated, leader, regState>>

LowerCapacity ==
    /\ free >= Step
    /\ capacity' = capacity - Step
    /\ free' = free - Step
    /\ UNCHANGED <<allocated, leader, regState>>

    \/ \E r \in Registrars : WinElection(r)
    \/ \E r \in Registrars : Fail(r)
    \/ \E r \in Registrars : Enroll(r)
    \/ \E r \in Registrars : Drop(r)
    \/ RaiseCapacity
    \/ LowerCapacity

CONSTANTS
    Registrars = {n1, n2, n3}
    None = None
    MaxCap = 4
    Step = 1
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SeatConservation
nl:
A university course-registration system manages the seats of one course through a set of registrar nodes, of which only an elected leader may change enrollments. When there is no leader a registrar can win the election and become leader, and a leader can fail, vacating the role so a failover election picks a new one. The course capacity changes at runtime: the registrar's office can raise capacity, which adds exactly that many free seats, or lower it when enough seats are free, which removes exactly that many free seats. The leader enrolls a student by moving one seat from free to allocated, and processes a drop by moving one seat from allocated back to free. Every one of these operations moves seats between the free and allocated pools or adjusts both capacity and free together by the same amount, so no seat is ever created or destroyed. The count of free seats plus the count of allocated seats must therefore always equal the current capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of free seats plus the number of allocated seats always equals the current course capacity, so seats are conserved across enrollments, drops, and capacity changes.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Stations, Bays, None, MaxAllocs

VARIABLES token, owner, holds, crashed, allocs

vars == <<token, owner, holds, crashed, allocs>>

Init ==
    /\ token \in Stations
    /\ owner = [b \in Bays |-> None]
    /\ holds = [s \in Stations |-> None]
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ allocs = 0

PassToken(t) ==
    /\ t # token
    /\ t \notin crashed
    /\ token' = t
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, holds, crashed, allocs>>

Crash(s) ==
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ s \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, owner, holds, allocs>>

Claim(s, b) ==
    /\ token = s
    /\ s \notin crashed

Because every update is routed to exactly one field and adds its weight there just once, each field's value always equals the summed weights of exactly the updates routed to it, so no update is ever lost or double-counted.
